5.19.10.en: Origen The Lord delivers man from the swords of enemies, however many they may be, so that the wars of the demons cannot destroy us. "A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee" (Ps 91:7).

5.19.11.en: * Jesus, the Son of God, my Lord, gives me and commands me to crush under my feet the spirit of fornication, and to tread upon the neck of the spirit of wrath and anger, and the demon of greed, etc.

5.19.12.en: * As the Father [only hath immortality] (1 Tim 6:16), the Lord Jesus, out of love for us, took upon Himself the burden of death on our behalf.

5.19.13.en: And in the same manner this description applies to the Father alone: "In him is no darkness." For Christ, for the benefit of men, took upon Himself our darkness, so that by His authority He might bring our death to naught and dispel our inner darkness.

5.19.14.en: * Before the coming of our Lord and Savior, all the demons reigned over the minds and bodies of men, and settled in their spirits. Then the grace of the Lord the Savior and His mercy appeared on the earth, teaching us how the soul of every man should regain freedom and recover the image of God in which it was created...

5.19.15.en: Who is this, if not Jesus Christ, by whose stripes we who believe in Him have been healed, when He "spoiled principalities and powers" who were in our midst and "made a shew of them openly" upon the Cross? (Col 15:2).

5.19.16.en: * We fell under the authority of our enemies, that is, "the king of this age" and his helpers from the powers of evil. For this reason arose our need for redemption by Him who buys us so that we may return from the state of estrangement from Him. Therefore our Savior gave His blood as a ransom for us...

5.19.17.en: And since the "remission of sins," which follows redemption, is impossible before man is set free, we must first be freed from the authority of him who took us captive and kept us under his control, freed beyond the reach of his hand, so that we may be able to obtain forgiveness of our sins and healing from the wounds of sin, so that we may accomplish works of godliness and other virtues.

5.20.0.en: Origen Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh [21].

5.20.1.en: As God protects His children from the sword in battle, so He protects them from the tongue of the wicked, which is sharper than the sword; He protects them from the accusations and slanders falsely directed at them. Thus in time of war as in time of peace the believer lives under the shelter of God in peace, not fearing destruction, even if he sees it coming.

5.20.2.en: Eliphaz presents an accusation against Job in the form of advice: "Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh." As if he says: You were defeated in the trial, for when affliction came upon you, you should not have sinned with your tongue, but hidden yourself from this error. Your tongue bears witness to your snare, for you fell into the snare of the tongue, and bowed to its deadly scourges. Eliphaz did not know that what he says does not apply to Job, for God Himself bears witness that in all this he did not sin, nor charge God foolishly (Job 22:1); rather the one who fell into the snares of the tongue and under its scourges is Eliphaz himself, who wanted by them to make righteous Job fall. But to Job applies the saying of the psalmist: [For he shall deliver thee from the snare of the hunter, and from the harsh word] (Ps 3:91).

5.20.3.en: * The saints of the Lord loved keeping silence, for they realized that the voice of man is the beginning of sin. So the saint of the Lord said within himself: "I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue." For he knew, from what he had read before, that one of the signs of God's protection of man is that he hides from the scourges of his tongue and from the witness of his conscience.

5.20.4.en: We are disciplined by the rebukes of our thoughts, and the judgment of conscience.

5.20.5.en: We are also disciplined by the scourges of our voices, when we utter things that strike our souls with deadly blows, and our mind is struck with bloody wounds. But where is the man whose heart has been cleansed of the impurities of sin, so that he does not sin with his tongue?

5.20.6.en: Thus, seeing that there is no one who could keep his mouth free from evil speech, he set for himself the rule of righteousness by committing himself to the ordinances of silence. He set before his eyes to avoid by silence the fall which it was hard for him to escape by speech.

5.21.0.en: St. Ambrose * [Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh] [22]. For when the saints see themselves engaged with the adversary in various forms, they equip themselves in different ways for their battle.

5.21.1.en: They have the help of the Word of God against famine.

5.21.2.en: And they have the armor of self-control against the sword of war.

5.21.3.en: And they have the fortress of patience against the scourge of the tongue.

5.21.4.en: And they have the help of inner love against the harm of outward calamities.

5.21.5.en: Thus in a wonderful way they pass through the various trials the wicked enemy brings upon them, and so gain greater riches in virtue as soldiers of God.

5.21.7.en: * "Thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction" (Jer 5:3). God in His providence and mercy, when He does His purifying work for the salvation of the soul, goes in His work to the end (to consumption), at least on His part. So if all that comes upon us from divine providence aims at our perfection and our discipline, and yet we do not accept the divine disciplines that lead us to perfection, then he who understands the meaning of this passage can say to the Lord: O Lord, You have consumed them (disciplined them), and they refused to receive correction.

5.21.8.en: Origen At destruction and dearth (famine) thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth [22].

5.21.9.en: The believer looks at the plots of the wicked and the raging of the beasts of the wilderness, and in tranquility makes light of them, for he is kept in God. Such was the Apostle Paul, who did not fear the last enemy, which is death, and completed his hymn saying: "O death, where is thy sting?" (1 Cor 15:55), "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us" (Rom 8:37).

5.21.10.en: * [At destruction and famine he shall laugh]... It was well said by the psalmist: [The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him: Lo, the man that made not God his helper] (Ps 6:52-7). Now the righteous look at the wicked and fear, and afterward they look and laugh. They are now held by fear lest they imitate them, but since they cannot reform those who have fallen under the eternal judgment, they do not harbor sympathy for them.

5.21.12.en: * You find many passages in Holy Scripture in which God is likened to the attributes of man. So if you ever hear the words "the wrath and fury of God," do not think that wrath and fury are emotions and attributes found in God, but they are a way by which God condescends and speaks to discipline His children and correct them.

5.21.13.en: For we too, when we wish to guide our children and correct their errors, appear before them in a fearsome guise and with a stern and firm face that does not match our true feelings, but matches the method of discipline.

5.21.14.en: If we showed on our faces the tolerance and leniency that is in our souls and inner feelings toward our children all the time, without changing the features of our faces according to the children's behavior, we would spoil them and drive them to the worse. In this way we speak of the wrath of God; when it is said that God is angry, what is meant by this wrath is your repentance and reformation, because God in His reality is neither angry nor furious, but you are the one who will bear the effects of wrath and fury when you fall into terrible, harsh torments because of your sins and evils, in the case of God's disciplining you by what we call the wrath of God!

5.22.0.en: Origen For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee [23].

5.22.1.en: When the believer is at peace with God he has friendship with all creation. He makes a covenant even with the stones of the field, so that he does not strike his foot against a stone. He makes a covenant of peace even with the beasts of the wilderness. "And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and with the fowls of heaven, and with the creeping things of the ground: and I will break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the earth, and will make them to lie down safely" (Hos 2:18). Whoever is in covenant with the Creator of heaven and earth, heaven and earth desire to be reconciled with him and find pleasure in serving him.

5.22.2.en: * Thus it is obligatory for us to struggle, and to amend our errors, and to correct our conduct, for without doubt when this is done uprightly we come to be in a much better state even with the predatory animals and beasts, not to speak of human beings.

5.22.3.en: This agrees with what is recorded in the book of blessed Job: [The wild beasts shall be at peace with thee] (Job 5:23) LXX. You will not fear attacks that come from outside, and a stumbling block outside will not be able to affect us as long as its roots are not allowed to enter and be planted in us. For [great peace have they which love thy name, and they have no stumbling block] (Ps 165:119).

5.22.4.en: St. John Cassian * [And the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with thee] [23]. It is clear that the demons were subject to him, not by their will, but under compulsion. For he understands all this with courage and patience... He knows how to guard his house in peace, since Job's body was not in conflict against the spirit (1 Cor 16:3), and the passions of the flesh did not resist the law of the Spirit.

5.22.5.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Our deceitful enemy is called "the beast of the earth," for he violently preys with his savage nature, seizing the souls of sinners at the hour of their death... But the righteous, since they submit with all their hearts to the fear of God, all the burden of fear from the adversary is removed from them.

5.22.6.en: * "The Truth" gave peace to His disciples at the beginning when He said: [Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you] (Jn 27:14). Simeon desired perfect peace when he asked Him, saying: [Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word] (Lk 29:2). For our peace begins with our longing for the Creator, and is completed by the clear vision. It will be perfect when our minds are no longer blinded by ignorance, nor affected by bodily assaults. For when we touch it in its beginnings, either the soul is subject to God or the body is subject to the soul, so it is said of the tabernacle of the righteous man that it is in peace, that is, in his body in which his mind dwells, so that the rebellious emotions and those of the lusts are under the guidance of the hand of righteousness.

5.23.0.en: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt lose nothing [24].

5.23.1.en: In reconciliation with God peace is achieved in the home and the family. He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High (Ps 91:1), the Most High dwells in his house, and cares for the salvation of his family.

5.23.2.en: What is the tabernacle but the body that is sanctified by the Lord Christ, and so becomes glorified and secure on an eternal level?

5.23.3.en: * We do not want to be rid of the body, but of the corruption in it. Our body is a burden to us, not because it is a body but because it is corruptible and subject to suffering. But when the new life comes, it removes this corruption - I say this corruption, not the body itself.

5.23.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * Moses the prophet showed us as an example, by the glory of the Spirit that shone on his face which no one could look steadily upon, how in the resurrection of the righteous the bodies of those who are worthy will be glorified, with a glory which the holy and faithful souls already obtain from now, being counted worthy to possess this glory within them, in the inner man.

5.23.5.en: St. Macarius the Great * They justly receive the reward of their sufferings in the body in which the righteous suffered and grieved and were approved by sufferings by every means. And in the same body in which they were killed for their love of God, in it they will live, and in the same body in which they endured slavery, in it they will reign.

5.24.0.en: St. Irenaeus Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth [25].

5.24.1.en: Job lost all his children, and here Eliphaz tells him that if he returns to God his seed will multiply and his offspring will flourish.

5.24.2.en: The offspring of the righteous are many like the grass of the earth, for God gives the righteous word and grace, so they win many souls to the Lord as children for Him.

5.24.3.en: * When we are completely subject to God, we are also supplied with the word of preaching. And a great offspring succeeds the souls of believers when they are first granted holy preaching... The offspring of the righteous man is compared to the grass of the earth, because whoever is born in an image of him, while the corruption of the glory of the present time is removed, becomes green with hope in eternal things.

5.25.0.en: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season [26].

5.25.1.en: Returning to God grants him length of days, so he completes his mission and enters the grave in a good old age at the proper time, as wheat is gathered and stored in its season.

5.25.2.en: * [Thou shalt come to thy grave in fullness (of old age), like a shock (heap) of wheat in its season]. What does he mean by the grave but the contemplative life, which as it were buries us, who are dead to the world, and hides us in the inner world far from earthly lusts. For those who are dead to the outward life are also buried in contemplation, those to whom Paul says: "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God" (Col 3:3)...

5.25.3.en: So he who subdues the arrogance of the flesh in himself leaves for it this work: to train the mind with holy exercises. And he who opens his mind in the holy words is exalted and extends, enjoying inner contemplation. For he is not a perfect preacher who devotes himself to contemplation, neglecting the obligation of the work entrusted to him, or who because of the obligation of work leaves the obligation of contemplation...

5.25.4.en: By contemplation they rise in the love of God, and by preaching they return to the service of their neighbor...

5.25.5.en: The time of work comes first and afterward contemplation. Therefore every perfect man must begin by training his thought in virtuous habits and afterward lie down in the heaps of the wheat of rest... "Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee" (Lk 39:8)... After we are healed the Lord sends us to our home. He commands us to relate the things He has done with us, so that the soul may first be occupied with work and afterward be refreshed by contemplation. Accordingly Jacob served for Rachel and obtained Leah. And it was said to him: [It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn] (Gen 26:29)... What is meant by Rachel but the contemplative life?

5.25.7.en: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is;

5.26.0.en: hear it, and know thou it for thyself [27].

5.26.1.en: As Eliphaz brought out the goodness of God who receives the repentant to restore to them their peace, happiness and good things, he concludes his first speech by offering a sure guarantee of his wisdom which he presented to Job.

5.26.2.en: We have received faith in God through holy tradition; this does not mean our slackness, but we must search for Him and ask that He be manifested in our life, and get to know Him each day, so that we love Him and possess Him. We listen to His voice and learn from Him so that we may have personal experience in dealing with Him.

5.26.3.en: He asks Job to search into what he has heard concerning the beasts of the earth, the heaps of wheat and the grave, so as not to take the meanings literally, but to perceive their deep spiritual mysteries and so enjoy contemplation of God.

5.26.4.en: * That is, be a judge of yourself, with the verdict to your conscience face to face. But Job's works are shining, and his hidden thoughts are more radiant than his visible works, and this during the battle the enemy stirred up against him.

5.26.6.en: You are the mystery of blessedness!

5.26.7.en: * A desire I desired, to abide in You forever.

5.26.8.en: You are the resurrection and the eternal life.

5.26.9.en: I possess You, and so I enjoy the mystery of the blessed eternal life.

5.26.10.en: * My heart is lifted up to enjoy the fellowship of the saints.

5.26.11.en: In their love they pray for me, and ask for the salvation of my soul.

5.26.12.en: But what is the benefit of their prayers unless I return to You by repentance?

5.26.13.en: How can I share their portion unless I respond to the riches of Your grace?

5.26.14.en: * Sin deprived me of enjoying You, O eternal Love.

5.26.15.en: It removed love from me, and so anger and envy took possession of me.

5.26.16.en: I turned to folly and ignorance, and so I became dry.

5.26.17.en: Sin uprooted me from my roots, so I no longer dwell in You, O mystery of life.

5.26.18.en: I was deprived of inner peace and true security.

5.26.19.en: In folly I stumbled at You, O divine Door.

5.26.20.en: The enemy scattered my gifts, and shattered my energies.

5.26.21.en: I became food for him, and drink for his evil angels.

5.26.22.en: My life turned into a wilderness filled with thorns and thistles.

5.26.23.en: I confess all the bitterness that has befallen me.

5.26.24.en: It is the fruit of my negligence and ignorance!

5.26.25.en: Who will rescue me from the enemy, and carry me to You, but Your rich grace?

5.26.26.en: * Now I return to You, seeking Your presence within me.

5.26.27.en: You are the Worker of wonders; by Your Holy Spirit renew my nature, and raise up from my dry wilderness a spiritual paradise.

5.26.28.en: Transform my earth into heaven, and my weak humanity into a heavenly life.

5.26.29.en: Fill me with Your Holy Spirit, the heavenly rain; let Him carry me on His two wings and fly with me to the divine embraces.

5.26.30.en: Let Him lift me up to the heights, and there my soul will rest.

5.26.31.en: Make me a wonder, O Wonderful One!

5.26.32.en: * Discipline me, for I am Your son, the object of Your surpassing care.

5.26.33.en: Let Your hands crush me, and heal me.

5.26.34.en: Allow six troubles, and in the seventh deliver me.

5.26.35.en: Allow hunger, that You may give me Yourself as heavenly bread.

5.26.36.en: Let the enemy strike with his sword; it will turn back upon him, for I am in Your embrace.

5.26.37.en: Let my tongue be silent, for my heart converses with You.

5.26.38.en: Would that the evil world collapse, for I am awaiting Your coming on the clouds.

5.26.39.en: Let me lean on Your breast, and I will not fear the ravening beasts of the wilderness.

5.26.40.en: Dwell in me and I in You, that my body may be sanctified with my mind and soul.

5.26.41.en: Let the tabernacle of my body be in security, and let its holy fruits be blessed by Your Holy Spirit.

5.26.42.en: Let me live all the days of my sojourn in Your might, and with joy let me depart, satisfied with the days which You have blessed.
